title: Repair a node table
hints: The key needs two parts: `op`, and something that says which sources.
`tuple(n.id for n in src)` turns the list of source nodes into a tuple of their ids. A tuple can be a dict key and a list can't.
On a hit, return `table[key]`. That is the very same object as before, which is what `is` checks.
prompt:
This make is almost a hash-consing table. Two lines are wrong.

The key. It only looks at the op, so add of two different pairs of sources would collide. It should be the op plus the ids of the sources, as a tuple.

The hit. When the key is already in the table it builds a new node anyway. It should hand back the node that is stored there.

answer.explain: The key `(op, tuple(n.id for n in src))` says exactly which node this is: the same op on the same sources. When that key is already in the table, returning `table[key]` hands back the one node that was built the first time, so nothing is ever built twice.

tests.expr: (mk := create(), x := mk('x', []), mk('add', [x, x]) is mk('add', [x, x]))[-1]
(mk := create(), x := mk('x', []), y := mk('y', []), mk('add', [x, y]) is mk('add', [y, x]))[-1]
(mk := create(), x := mk('x', []), mk('neg', [x]) is mk('neg', [x, x]))[-1]
(mk := create(), last := mk('c', []), [last := mk('s', [last]) for _ in range(1000)], mk('s', [mk('c', [])]).id)[-1]
